claim: An ensemble of three orthogonal code-specific uncertainty axes (lexical/token entropy, algorithmic/pseudo-code consistency, functional/execution consistency) improves average AUROC from 0.696 (strongest NL-derived baseline) to 0.776 across five code LLMs.
stance_target: value of code-specific (vs NL-inherited) uncertainty signals for correctness discrimination
scope_conditions: five code LLMs, whole-generation scalar AUROC discrimination
quoted_support: An ensemble of the three axes improves average AUROC from 0.696 (strongest NL-derived baseline) to 0.776 (+8.1 points) across five code LLMs

claim: On Qwen3-14B, single-pass Top-K token entropy alone matches the strongest multi-pass uncertainty baseline at more than 3x lower inference cost.
stance_target: cost-efficiency tradeoffs among code uncertainty estimation methods
quoted_support: on Qwen3-14B, single-pass Top-K token entropy alone matches the strongest multi-pass baseline at >3x lower cost

claim: This work produces an inference-time ensemble of uncertainty signals as a single scalar per-problem/per-generation score, not a per-test-case dense confidence vector, and involves no SFT/RL training of the model to natively express confidence.
stance_target: DPRC's differentiation on granularity and training-vs-inference-time mechanism
quoted_support: this is an INFERENCE-TIME ensemble of UE signals producing a single scalar per-problem/per-generation score (evaluated via AUROC discrimination), not a per-test-case dense confidence vector; it is not a training method
